Hi Emily — thanks for the context and the report. Quick read-through shows clear weekly peaks (~3x baseline) with sustained mid-day traffic. Two practical options based on what you described:

Option 1 — Upgrade to Pro tier (recommended if you want fewer operational changes):
- Pro includes route-level SLOs, advanced KV/prefix caching, and priority routing.
- Predictable monthly cost; licensing covers the features you noted.
- Add-on: burst-dedicated pools (billed as committed capacity) for headroom on peak days.

Option 2 — Keep current tier + buy Dedicated throughput credits:
- Lower baseline cost but more variable spend during peak weeks.
- You maintain current feature set; advanced caching can be added as an a la carte feature for a smaller monthly fee.

For a 12-month commitment we usually layer a volume discount starting at 15% for $X committed spend, rising to 22% for larger commitments. Ben, can you confirm the current discount schedule and whether we can offer an introductory pilot credit for the first month?

Next steps I suggest: 1) I’ll draft a side-by-side price sketch for the two options (monthly burned tokens + burst credits), 2) Ben will outline discount and pilot credit possibilities, and 3) if procurement wants, Kar is available to field any SLA/contract redlines. Can you confirm which internal team will own billing vs. who signs the contract?

—Olga

Emily — looped in per Olga. A few specifics on pricing and discounts to help make the CFO math easier:

- Baseline: Pro tier list price is $7,500/month and includes up to 8M tokens/month + the feature set Olga described.
- Dedicated throughput credits: $0.60 per 1k effective token-equivalent when purchased as on-demand top-up; committed buckets start at $30k/month and slide to $0.45 per 1k depending on volume.
- Add-on advanced caching: $1,200/month if added to current tier (not necessary if you pick Pro).

Discounting (12-month term):
- Commit $90k/year (our entry enterprise band) => 15% off list.
- Commit $180k/year => 20% off.
- Commit $360k/year => 25% off + 1 month free at renewal.

Pilot credit: we can offer a 20% credit on incremental spend for the first 30 days of an upgrade to Pro (applies only to new capacity purchased for the pilot).

If it helps, I can produce a simple TCO calc comparing staying + credits vs upgrading to Pro given Emily's usage (Olga, can you drop the Q1 numbers into a quick model?).

Hi Emily / Procurement team —

Short answers:
1) Pro list price assumes single-region hosted (US). Multi-region adds a regional replication premium; typical uplift is ~18% for active-active across two regions (we can provide an exact number once you confirm regions).
2) Committed discounts apply to overall committed spend; additional dedicated credits purchased on top will tier down in price once you hit the higher committed bands. In short: yes, you get combined benefits as you cross thresholds.
3) Pilot credit: we can apply the 30-day pilot credit to add-on features in dev as long as the pilot capacity is tagged and scoped in the purchase order.

Attached is a short SLA excerpt and renewal/cancellation language (excerpted). If procurement has specific redlines, send them to contracts@redwood.com and I’ll triage.
